alex: quick heads up — after the quantized Llama roll out latency spiked on 2k tokens. I'm seeing different kernel choices mid-request, looks like a switch after KV refill.
alex: ran a short nsys capture, here's command I used:
alex: ```
nsys profile --trace=cuda,nvtx,osrt --output=run_q2k --capture-range=nvtx --duration=6 --sample=cpu --sample-interval=100ms -- ./serve_local --model=llama-q8
```
alex: attached the timeline but curious if I'm missing flags to capture the kernel handoff/windows more cleanly — sample window maybe cutting off transitions? :thinking:
mira: try bracketed NVTX around the whole generate loop and extend duration. also include --trace=cudamanager? (not sure) but nvtx/osrt are key.
mira: e.g. wrap request path with nvtx ranges so capture only hot path. shorter capture often misses kernel tail.
mira: command tweak:
mira: ```
nsys profile --trace=cuda,nvtx,osrt --output=run_q2k_bracket --capture-range=nvtx --duration=12 --sample=cpu --sample-interval=50ms -- ./serve_local --model=llama-q8
```
dan: also enable timeline markers: insert NVTX markers at kv-load/kv-evict points. that'll show exact kernel mapping to kv-cache ops.
dan: if kernel choice flips between matmul kernels and fused attention, check warmup vs steady-state tokens — kernels differ by seq len and batch packing.
riley: fwiw i saw similar — it was batching heuristics where small tail batches fell back to a different kernel; increase min_batch_delay or force consistent batch sizing for test.
alex: good call, I can repro with a deterministic micro-bench: send 1 request of 2k tokens, then 100 requests of varying lens, compare timelines.
perf-bot: nsys report generated at /tmp/run_q2k_bracket.qdrep, flamegraph at /tmp/run_q2k_bracket.sqlite :mag:
alex: excellent — next steps: run with NVTX-bracketed capture + longer duration, replicate with/without kv-prefetch, and collect two runs to diff kernel timelines.
mira: also capture a short perf counter sample (sm__throughput?), nsys metrics can be noisy but helps spot memory-bound kernels vs compute-bound.
dan: if you want low overhead, use sample interval >50ms and avoid tracing API calls you don't need. OR use osrt capture to see sampler boundaries.
alex: thanks all — i'll drop the qdrep and sqlite here when done and ping for a quick look. :thumbsup:
